name: LTC1751EMS8-5#PBF
title: LTC1751 family: micropower regulated charge pump doubler, 3.3 V, 5 V or adjustable output
summary: The LTC1751, LTC1751-3.3 and LTC1751-5 are inductorless step-up converters: a switched-capacitor voltage doubler with burst regulation that holds its output at 3.3 V, 5 V or a resistor-set level from an input of 2 V to 5.5 V. Only a flying capacitor and input and output bypass capacitors are needed outside. The fixed versions deliver up to 100 mA (5 V, VIN at least 3 V) or 80 mA (3.3 V, VIN at least 2.5 V), draw about 20 µA unloaded and under 2 µA in shutdown, and cut the output off from the input when shut down. They add a power-good output, an SS pin for soft-start, short-circuit and thermal protection, and come in an 8-lead MSOP.

notes: The three versions share one pinout except pin 1: the fixed-output parts bring out the power-good flag there, the adjustable part its feedback input. Parts for a wider temperature range are available on request to the factory.

pins.name: PGOOD
pins.function: LTC1751-3.3 and LTC1751-5 only. Power-good flag: held low at start-up until VOUT comes within about 4.5% of its regulated value, then released to high impedance; pulled low again if VOUT later sags about 7% under regulation. Needs a pull-up resistor to whatever logic rail suits.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: LTC1751 (adjustable) only. Feedback input, compared against the internal 1.205V reference to regulate the output; a resistor divider from VOUT to this pin sets the output voltage.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Regulated output. Bypass it with a low-ESR capacitor of at least 6.8µF placed as near the pin as can be managed.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input. Bypass it with a low-ESR capacitor of at least 6.8µF.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground; connect to a ground plane for best results.

pins.name: SHDN
pins.function: Shutdown input, active low: a low level turns the part off. It must always be driven, never left open.

pins.name: SS
pins.function: Soft-start: a capacitor from this pin sets how fast the output ramps at turn-on, keeping the start-up input surge down.

circuits.title: Regulated 5V output from a 2.7V to 5.5V input
circuits.description: LTC1751-5 doubling a 2.7V to 5.5V input to a regulated 5V ±4%, good for 100mA with VIN at least 3V or 50mA with VIN at least 2.7V. C2 bypasses the input, C1 the output, CFLY is the pump capacitor across C+ and C-. SHDN is the on/off control. R1 pulls the open-drain PGOOD flag up to VOUT. SS is left open.
notes: IOUT ≤ 100mA with VIN ≥ 3V; IOUT ≤ 50mA with VIN ≥ 2.7V.

circuits.title: Output ripple reduction (Figure 1)
circuits.description: An RC stage after the output of an LTC1751-X: the regulator's output capacitor, a 1Ω series resistor and a second capacitor form a low-pass that removes the high-frequency charge-transfer spikes before the 5V load.

circuits.title: Programming the adjustable LTC1751 (Figure 3)
circuits.description: The adjustable part's output set by R1 from VOUT to FB and R2 from FB to GND, giving VOUT = 1.205V(1 + R1/R2); COUT is the output capacitor.

circuits.title: USB port to regulated 5V supply with soft-start
circuits.description: An LTC1751-5 run from a USB port's supply. The port feeds VIN through a 1Ω resistor, with 10µF at VIN after it; SHDN is tied to VIN so the converter is always on. A 1nF capacitor on SS gives a soft-start ramp to hold down the inrush the port sees. Output is 5V on a 10µF capacitor, and a 100k pull-up to VOUT serves the PGOOD flag.

circuits.title: 2-cell NiCd or NiMH to 3.3V with low standby current
circuits.description: An LTC1751-3.3 making 3.3V at 40mA from two NiCd or NiMH cells. 10µF capacitors bypass input and output and a 1µF capacitor is the flying capacitor. SHDN takes an external on/off signal. 1nF on SS sets the soft-start, and 100k from VOUT pulls PGOOD up.

circuits.title: Boosted constant current source
circuits.description: The adjustable LTC1751 regulating current instead of voltage: the load sits between VOUT and FB, and RX from FB to ground senses its current, so the loop holds 1.205V across RX and IL = 1.205V/RX, as long as the needed VOUT stays at or below 2VIN. 10µF bypasses VIN and VOUT, 1µF is the flying capacitor, SHDN is the on/off control and SS is unused.

circuits.title: Low power battery backup with auto switchover and no reverse current
circuits.description: A 5V rail kept alive from a 3-cell NiCd pack. While the 5V input is present, P-channel MOSFET Q1 (Si4435DY) connects it straight to VOUT and the pack trickle-charges through D1 and 75k. An LTC1540 comparator watches the input through the 1.43M/475k divider against its reference, with hysteresis set by 10k and 1M; it is powered from the higher of battery and VOUT through the BAT54C dual Schottky. When the input fails, the comparator output goes high: it turns Q1 off, so no current flows back into the input, and enables the LTC1751-5 through SHDN, which then makes 5V (up to 100mA) from the battery. 330pF on SS sets the soft-start. PGOOD, pulled to VOUT by 100k, reads high in backup mode.
notes: D1 is marked IN4148; the part is the 1N4148.

circuits.title: Current mode white or blue LED driver with PWM brightness control
circuits.description: The adjustable LTC1751 driving up to six white or blue LEDs from a 3V to 4.5V Li-Ion cell. Each LED has its own 82Ω ballast resistor to ground; the first LED's resistor is also the sense resistor on FB, so the loop holds 1.205V across it and the other strings follow. Brightness is set by pulse-width modulating SHDN with a 17ms period. C1 and C2 (10µF) bypass input and output, C4 (1µF) is the flying capacitor and C3 (680pF) on SS sets the soft-start.

operation.text: A switched-capacitor doubler raises VIN. An internal divider (external on the adjustable part) feeds comparator COMP1; when the divided output falls under its lower threshold the pump runs, driven by a two-phase non-overlapping clock. In the first phase the flying capacitor charges to VIN; in the second it is placed in series with VIN and dumps into VOUT. Pumping goes on at the clock rate until the upper threshold is reached, then stops. While stopped the part takes under 20µA typical, which keeps light-load efficiency high (Burst Mode operation).

A logic low on SHDN turns all circuitry off; the input then supplies only leakage, and VOUT is disconnected from VIN. SHDN is a CMOS gate input switching at about 0.8V. Driving it high with a level below VIN raises quiescent current slightly compared with driving it fully to VIN. Because it is high impedance it must always be held at a valid logic level, never left floating. SS is pulled to ground while SHDN is low.

A doubler's input current is about twice its output current, so it behaves like a linear regulator fed from 2VIN: efficiency is close to VOUT/(2VIN). The low-power design keeps efficiency good down to fairly light loads.

With VOUT shorted the part pulls 200mA to 400mA from VIN and heats up. Thermal shutdown stops the pump at roughly 160°C junction and restarts it near 150°C; the part cycles this way indefinitely, without latch-up or damage, until the short is removed.

Capacitor type and value set output ripple, pump strength and minimum start-up time. Use low-ESR (< 0.1Ω) ceramic or tantalum parts of 6.8µF or more for CIN and COUT; aluminum electrolytics have too much ESR. If the source feeding VIN is low impedance up to several MHz, CIN can be omitted or made smaller, at the cost of more ripple on VIN. A larger COUT (10µF or more) lowers output ripple but lengthens the minimum turn-on time and raises start-up current.

Never use a polarized (tantalum or aluminum) flying capacitor: its voltage can reverse at start-up. Use low-ESR ceramic. Its value sets pump strength: at least 0.6µF of real capacitance is needed for rated output current, so allow for loss with temperature and voltage. X7R holds its value well from -40°C to 85°C; Z5U and Y5V lose much of it over temperature and can drop 50% or more at rated voltage. An X7R of 1µF minimum is the usual choice; for very light loads 0.01µF to 0.68µF can be used, which lowers output ripple but also maximum output current and efficiency.

Two components. A low-frequency sawtooth comes from comparator hysteresis and control delays; its size and rate depend on load, VIN and COUT. At high VIN the stronger pump can overshoot in one cycle instead of bursting, and the average output creeps up; a larger COUT keeps it bursting. A high-frequency spike appears during each charging phase, equal to charging current times COUT's ESR, and grows with VIN, flying capacitance and ESR. Typical total ripple for an LTC1751-5 at VIN = 3V and full load is 75mVP-P with a 10µF low-ESR output capacitor; a smaller COUT or heavier load increases it.

For VIN above 3.3V or ripple under 100mVP-P, use COUT of 22µF or more, which lowers both ripple components through slower slew and lower ESR. A low-ESR ceramic COUT cuts the spikes but only a large value cuts the sawtooth. An RC filter after VOUT (Figure 1: 1Ω with 10µF tantalum on each side) also removes the spikes. A larger output capacitor lengthens the minimum turn-on time.

About 2µA flows out of SS into its capacitor; the regulation loop follows the resulting ramp until the output is in regulation, limiting inrush from VIN. The capacitor is optional: without it the output rises as fast as the pump allows, at a rate set by temperature, load, pump and flying capacitor values and VIN.

On the fixed versions PGOOD has two jobs. After SHDN goes high, VOUT follows the SS ramp and PGOOD stays low until VOUT reaches regulation (the UVH threshold, -4.5% of nominal), then goes high impedance. If VOUT is later dragged down by overload to the UVL threshold (-7% of nominal), PGOOD pulls low again; with a short holding VOUT down it never releases. Figure 2 shows SHDN, PGOOD and VOUT through a normal start-up, with tr measured from 10% to 90%, and then an undervoltage event. The pull-up may go to any available supply, VOUT included; an unused PGOOD can be tied to GND.

The adjustable LTC1751 sets VOUT with an external divider from VOUT to FB to GND (Figure 3); the fixed parts have the divider inside. Output cannot exceed twice the input. Large divider values keep quiescent current low.
Model the adjustable part as a 2VIN source behind its open-loop resistance ROUT (Figure 4) and use the lowest VIN; typical ROUT against VIN at 50mA and 100mA is in Figure 5.

The 800kHz switching and fast current edges call for a true ground plane and short traces to every capacitor; Figure 6 is the recommended arrangement, with VIN, VOUT and GND copper next to the package and the capacitors beside the pins.

At high VIN and full load the part can dissipate enough to reach the roughly 160°C thermal shutdown. Connect GND (pin 4) to plane copper and keep solid ground copper under the package on two layers to cut the thermal resistance considerably.
